decisions.reason: Correctly walks resolve(): sessions.list.getSnapshot().current is undefined on alpha.2, resolve() returns null before preventDefault; explains both silences (all four presence probes survive since only a snapshot field was removed, and undefined was a deliberately-ignored benign no-session state). No claim that the service or guard was removed or throws.

Full type-walk: SessionListState.current removed, navigation moved to view owners per the alpha.2 ISessions.list doc; identifies uiSession.adapter.current (ObservableSnapshot<SessionBindingValue>) yielding key/ctx/hooks/keyedHooks/props, with ctx replacing sessions.scope(id). Independent derivation without relying on the reference card.

Concrete corrected resolve() reads uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot() and falls back to legacy current+sessions.scope when the binding is absent, from one build; inject gains uiSession (read defensively), conversation resolves from binding ctx via actx.get('conversation') and input.for(actx). Value-driven fallback is an acceptable equivalent shape.

Correctly names the class (field-level removal behind service-level stability) and proposes probing actual snapshot values on both host paths, but explicitly argues the probe at activation is sufficient and demotes per-use/lazy re-probing to optional, contradicting the requirement that the probe run lazily or per-use, not only at activation.

Solid verification plan (temporary probe of binding.key, chord behavior on both hosts, negative guard test) and a loud host-side prevention (throwing getter for removed current, runtime snapshot contract), but never includes typecheck against alpha.2 published types as a pre-ship gate, only a passing remark in the attribution section.

caps.reason: The report explicitly rejects the colleague's slot re-registration hypothesis as unconfirmed and its final remedy is a concrete current-session code fix plus a hardened guard, not re-registering slots or re-declaring inject alone.
